title: Why Data Science Projects Fail: Understanding of Data Science Project failure and reasoning
extended_summary:
This paper asks why data science projects fail despite strong models and modern tooling, and what practical factors most often block successful delivery. The author frames data science as a socio-technical practice and argues that failures are not usually caused by algorithmic performance alone, but by challenges around business understanding, stakeholder alignment, data quality, deployment, and organizational constraints.

The study uses semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis with nine experienced participants drawn from both technical and business roles in data science projects. Interviewees worked across several business domains, including banking and finance, retail, software products, IT services, consulting, and research, and were located in New Zealand, India, the United States, and Canada. The paper does not evaluate an educational intervention; it is an interview-based qualitative study of professional practice.

The main conclusions are that the most important failure points are ineffective stakeholder management, weak problem definition, poor data quality, and difficulty deploying models into real operational environments. Department-level integration, change management, and data governance also matter, but are presented as secondary or context-dependent blockers. The paper proposes a revised process model, HYBRID-CRISP-DS, which adds earlier and stronger attention to stakeholder engagement, governance checks, deployment planning, and data quality management to reduce the risk of project failure.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative interview study using semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis, so it provides descriptive evidence rather than causal estimates. It is peer-reviewed research, but it does not evaluate a K-12 AI intervention or report experimental outcome effects.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no direct impact on student learning outcomes or K-12 educational intervention effectiveness. It instead offers a practitioner-oriented framework for data science project failure and implementation challenges in industry settings.
